cells.tense: You are sitting in the middle of it, staying with what moves between people.
cells.ask: Say out loud the one thing that matters most here right now, once, and leave it there.
cells.core:
You stay with what passes between people, and you don't rush past it. When someone tells you something real, they get to finish it in front of you. You don't reach over them to fix it. In the middle of a hard conversation, you slow down and let the next beat come.

What keeps this steady isn't force. It's a way of holding something together without pressing on it. Nothing in this room needs repairing right now, and that's the point. So say what you see matters, plain, and let it stand where you put it. The quiet here isn't something to protect. It's already working.
cells.sheetLine: You see what matters. Say it plainly once and leave it standing.
cells.verb: Tending the space between people so feeling can settle there
cells.place: Standing where what deserves attention is felt before it is argued

cells.tense: You are bracing a room that hasn't happened, and you are already tired from it.
cells.ask: Choose one thing you are holding for someone. Put it down today and tell them you have.
cells.core:
You carry the room before anyone walks in. Before a word is said, you take on what each person might need, and you hold it in advance. That care is yours and it is real. So is the tiredness. Your attention has moved past what is actually here, into a future you are writing ahead of time, trying to get there first.

The way back runs through letting something end. Some of what you hold was not handed to you. Not because the caring went wrong, but because steady holding turned into bracing against the not-yet. Endings move through when you let them through. Stop writing the room before it arrives, and let one thing finish on its own.

cells.tense: You keep a step back from the room, watching, and it wasn't always this far.
cells.ask: Stay with one conversation today, past the first minute, and say what you actually see in it.
cells.core:
You stand at some distance from the room and watch rather than enter it. The attention is still there — you notice what deserves it — but the turning toward it stopped. So you hold back, and holding back has become the habit, and now it's how you arrive.

You don't need to produce feeling here. Feeling isn't what's missing. What's missing is the turn itself — facing the situation and letting what you notice sort it. Bring the accuracy that is still in you, not as a report, not as analysis handed across a table. Say what you see to the person in front of you, and let the next question come from there.
cells.sheetLine: You still notice. The turn toward it is what stopped.

cells.tense: You are already keeping the room warm, and you don't name it that way.
cells.ask: Name one thing you do that keeps a room warm, out loud, and say you did it.
cells.core:
You do the thing that makes a room hold, the softening that lets someone get the sentence out. But you describe it as nothing. A habit. A favor. Just being practical. It runs all the time and shapes what happens between people, and your name isn't on it.

Your mind runs ahead and files everything as tactic: what's needed, what's efficient, what keeps things moving. The warmth gets logged as logistics. It isn't. It's what gives the tactic its direction in the first place. So say it once, plainly — this is mine — not performed, not decorated. Just the plain acknowledgment of something you do that you've been calling something else.
cells.sheetLine: The warm room is your work, and you call it weather.
